- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward surprise.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast at 80–85% of peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “mean reversion” correction: average last 5–7 true values and adjust forecast toward it.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (first 5–7 days); apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.33, 1.00, 0.33), model often misreads trend; use sentiment-weighted moving average (e.g., 0.7*recent + 0.3*previous) to smooth forecast.
